topic: Did you have a good day?

grammar_patterns.pattern: Did you have a good day? Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
examples: Did you have a good day? No!
Did you like the movie, Max?
Did you have lots of fun?
What did you watch last night? A movie.
What did you eat? Amy had some of my lunch.
What did Katie use in her English class? Her dictionary.
Where did you watch the movie? At home.
Where did the boys have a picnic? In the park.
Where did the girls play tennis? At the playground.
When did the movie end? At nine o'clock.
When did Katie have English class? At one o'clock.
When did you visit your cousins? Last week.
Did he walk to school yesterday? No, he didn't.
Did the children stay in tents? Yes.
Did the children use rope to make a bridge?

grammar_patterns.pattern: We had [noun], but I didn't have my [noun].
examples: First we had P.E., but I didn't have my P.E. clothes.
Next, we had math, but I didn't have my calculator.
Then we had lunch, but I didn't have my lunchbox.

phonics.description: The long u sound spelled oo, ue, and u_e.
chant: I look up at the moon.
